title: Slice 3 · Task 12 — Simulator walk-through
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 12: Simulator walk-through

- [ ] Write the step-by-step script (what to tap, what to see) covering a fresh install, household and locations, adding the two Task 8 items plus a case of water, using and adjusting lots, the Dashboard drill-in, an Expiring soon filter, and an export/restore round-trip.
- [ ] Run `swift test`, `xcodegen generate` and both builds; hand the script to Hampton and wait for his report. Fixes found here go in this task's commits.

**Done when:** Hampton confirms every step.

title: Slice 3 · Task 10 — Dashboard
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 10: Dashboard

- [ ] Food and water cards, each with days as a range (Decision 3), the amount on hand (kcal, gal) and the daily need. Water shows untreated non-potable gallons beside the figure, never inside it.
- [ ] Effective runway range with the limiting category called out, and a one-line reminder to plan around the low number.
- [ ] Focus next (Task 2), with each Caution, Inspect or Use soon lot opening its lot detail.
- [ ] Empty and problem states: no people ("Add your household to compute runway" linking to Settings), no lots ("Add your first item"), and lots missing calories or water volume linking to their products.
- [ ] Tapping a category card opens Inventory filtered to that category (Task 9).

**Done when:** the Dashboard with the sample pantry shows the same food, water and effective low/high as the fixture test, rounded down.

**Design:** docs/design.md → "Slice 3 screens" (S3 · Dashboard (3 tabs), S3 · Dashboard, no household). For behavior, the spec and this task win.


**Design exports:** docs/design/screens/"S3 · Dashboard (3 tabs).png" + canvas/S3-Dashboard.dc.html; docs/design/screens/"S3 · Dashboard, no household.png" + canvas/S3-Dash-NoHousehold.dc.html.
close_reason: Dashboard: hero range + weakest-link callout + bars + plan-around line, food/water cards with on-hand/need/non-potable chip and Inventory drill-in, Focus next rows, household/first-item prompts, missing-calories product list

title: Slice 3 · Task 11 — Backup in Settings
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 11: Backup in Settings

- [ ] Export: writes the JSON backup and opens the share sheet, named with the site and date.
- [ ] Restore: picks a file, shows what it contains (export date, counts of sites, lots and products) and what will be replaced, offers "Export current data first", then replaces everything (Task 4). The app reloads onto the restored default site.
- [ ] A file that isn't a readable backup shows the `BackupError` text and changes nothing.

**Done when:** export, erase-and-restore and a second export round-trip on the simulator with the same lots.

**Design:** docs/design.md → "Slice 3 screens" (S3 · Settings, S3 · Restore backup). For behavior, the spec and this task win.


**Design exports:** docs/design/screens/"S3 · Settings (scrolled).png" + canvas/S3-Settings.dc.html; docs/design/screens/"S3 · Restore backup.png" + canvas/S3-Restore.dc.html.
close_reason: Backup in Settings: export to share sheet as Hearthstock-<site>-<date>.json, restore with file summary + what's replaced + export-first + confirmation, reload onto restored default site, unreadable file shows BackupError text

title: Slice 3 · Task 8 — Add flow
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 8: Add flow

The spec's goal is a bulk item or an old can entered in under 15 seconds.

- [ ] One sheet: product (picker or new), quantity with a unit picker limited to the product's unit kind and an optional "× packs" multiplier (24 × 0.5 L → 3.17 gal), printed date (any date, past or future, or "No expiry"), acquired date (defaults to today, editable), packaging, location (last-used preselected, Decision 8), opened, notes.
- [ ] **Product draft, one save.** When the product is new, the sheet holds a product draft (a Core value type with a product's fields and no ID) instead of saving the product first. Save writes the product and the lot through the Task 4 transaction; Cancel discards the draft, so no orphan products are left behind. Slice 4's scanner fills the same draft from a barcode lookup, so this save path doesn't change. An existing product goes straight to a plain lot save.
- [ ] Conversion to the base unit happens on save with `Quantity.inBaseUnit()`; the sheet shows the stored amount ("= 3.17 gal") before saving.
- [ ] Save and add another keeps product-independent choices (location, acquired date) for the next entry.
- [ ] After saving, the new lot's state is visible on the confirmation, so a back-filled old can shows Caution or Expired right away.

**Done when:** Hampton can enter "20 lb white rice, garage, best-by 2025-03" and "6 cans black beans, printed 14 months ago" and see their states.

**Design:** docs/design.md → "Slice 3 screens" (S3 · Add lot, manual, S3 · Add lot, saved). For behavior, the spec and this task win.


**Design exports:** docs/design/screens/"S3 · Add lot, manual (scrolled).png" + canvas/S3-AddLot.dc.html; docs/design/screens/"S3 · Add lot, saved.png" + canvas/S3-AddSaved.dc.html.
close_reason: Add sheet: picker/new draft, units + packs with stored amount, printed date (day/month/none), acquired, packaging, last-used location, one-save product+lot, confirmation with state/why/runway effect; RunwayEffect + QuantityEntry + timeline in Core; 314 tests

title: Slice 3 · Task 9 — Inventory
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 9: Inventory

- [ ] Lots grouped by location or by category (segmented control), with search and an Expiring soon filter (Task 3). Each row: product name, quantity in a readable unit, location path when grouped by category, state badge (Good normal, Use soon a neutral badge with an amber clock, Caution and Inspect amber with Inspect's check prompt, Expired red; every badge pairs a word and an icon with its color, never color alone) and flag icons (missing date, power-dependent, humidity risk).
- [ ] Swipe to **Use**: enter an amount in any unit of the product's kind (count products prefill 1); over-consuming shows the available amount. Swipe to **Adjust**: set the remaining quantity directly, for corrections.
- [ ] Lot detail: every field, usable-by date, why it's in its state (printed date, profile, window, climate), and Edit, Delete (Decision 5) and Archive.
- [ ] Opening Inventory from a Dashboard category shows that category, with a visible way to clear the filter.

**Done when:** every lot in the sample pantry is findable by search and by location, and Use, Adjust, Edit and Delete each change the Dashboard live.

**Design:** docs/design.md → "Slice 3 screens" (S3 · Inventory, swipe + filter, S3 · Use / Adjust sheet, S3 · Lot detail). For behavior, the spec and this task win.


**Design exports:** docs/design/screens/"S3 · Inventory, swipe + filter.png" + canvas/S3-Inventory.dc.html; docs/design/screens/"S3 · Use Adjust sheet.png" + canvas/S3-UseSheet.dc.html; docs/design/screens/"S3 · Lot detail (scrolled).png" + canvas/S3-LotDetail.dc.html.
close_reason: Inventory: group toggle, search, Expiring soon + category chips, rows with badges and flags, Use/Adjust swipe sheet, lot detail with why/timeline/runway effect, edit item/product, used up, delete

title: Slice 3 · Task 7 — Product form
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 7: Product form

- [ ] Create and edit a product: name, category, unit kind (mass, volume, energy, count), calories per base unit with the per-package helper (Decision 6), potable water per base unit (prefilled 1 gal per gal for water by volume, with a "not potable" switch that clears it), shelf-life profile picked by name, optional barcode typed by hand. Role is fixed to supply in this slice.
- [ ] Unit kind can't change once the product has lots, since their quantities are stored in its base unit.
- [ ] A product picker: search existing products by name, most recently used first when the search is empty, with "New product" always one tap away.
- [ ] Editing a product says it affects every lot of that product.
- [ ] Opened from the Add flow for a new product, the form's Save hands the draft back to the Add sheet instead of writing it (Task 8 saves product and lot together). Opened to edit an existing product, Save writes it directly.

**Done when:** a product can be created inline from the Add flow and edited later from a lot.

**Design:** docs/design.md → "Slice 3 screens" (S3 · Product picker, S3 · Product form). For behavior, the spec and this task win.


**Design exports:** docs/design/screens/"S3 · Product picker.png" + canvas/S3-ProductPicker.dc.html; docs/design/screens/"S3 · Product form (scrolled).png" + canvas/S3-ProductForm.dc.html.
close_reason: ProductDraft (Core) + per-package helper; product picker (recent/search/new) and product form (new hands back draft, edit saves, unit kind locked with lots); 306 tests

title: Slice 3 · Task 5 — App shell and view-model pattern
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 5: App shell and view-model pattern

- [ ] A `TabView` with Dashboard, Inventory and Settings, replacing the smoke `ContentView`. `RootView`'s open-or-show-error behavior stays.
- [ ] One view-model pattern, used by every screen: `@MainActor @Observable`, started from `.task`, subscribing to `observeRunwayInputs(siteID:)` and holding the latest snapshot plus Core results. Cancelling the task ends the subscription.
- [ ] `today` is computed once in the app and refreshed when the app becomes active and when the calendar day changes, so a phone left open overnight moves lots from Good to Caution without a relaunch.
- [ ] Errors from a write show as an alert with the error text; a failed subscription shows the error in place of the screen's content.
- [ ] The DEBUG "Load sample pantry" button moves to a Developer section at the bottom of Settings (DEBUG builds only).

**Done when:** the app launches into the three tabs, each tab shows live data for the default site, and Release builds have no sample loader.
close_reason: Tab shell, RunwayInputsModel pattern, Today clock, error alert, DEBUG sample loader in Settings; 297 tests, Debug+Release build

title: Slice 3 · Task 6 — Settings: household and locations
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 6: Settings: household and locations

- [ ] Site name, editable, and the Use soon notice window in days (Decision 7).
- [ ] Household: add, edit and remove people (name, kcal/day defaulting to 2,000, water gal/day defaulting to 1.0).
- [ ] Locations as a tree: add, rename, move under a parent, set climate class (with "inherit from parent"), humidity, and the kit toggles (Decision 10). Show each class's multiplier and example spots from the spec's climate table as help text.
- [ ] Deleting a location that still holds lots, has children or is a kit shows why, using the typed `RepositoryError`s, instead of failing silently.

**Done when:** a new user can describe their household and storage without the sample loader.

**Design:** docs/design.md → "Slice 3 screens" (S3 · Settings, S3 · Edit location). For behavior, the spec and this task win.


**Design exports:** docs/design/screens/"S3 · Settings (scrolled).png" + canvas/S3-Settings.dc.html; docs/design/screens/"S3 · Edit location (scrolled).png" + canvas/S3-Location.dc.html.
close_reason: Settings: site name + notice stepper, household CRUD, location tree editor with climate/humidity/kit, typed delete errors; LocationTree in Core; 299 tests

title: Slice 3 · Task 4 — Store and data gaps
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 4: Store and data gaps

Small additions the screens need. Each one is listed in the plan before it's made.

- [ ] Migration `v2_site_notice_window`: the site's notice window as a column defaulting to 30, saved and loaded through `SiteRepository`. The backup format version goes up by one, and a version 1 file still imports with the default.
- [ ] `LotRepository.delete(_:)`: removes the lot and its shelf-life override; deleting a missing lot does nothing.
- [ ] `KitRepository.delete(_:)`: removes the kit and clears its location's kit link, so a location can stop being a kit and later be deleted.
- [ ] `ProductRepository.list()`, if `search(name: "")` isn't clear enough at the call site; otherwise note that `search` covers it.
- [ ] Shelf-life profiles gain a display `name` in `shelf-life-defaults.json` and `ShelfLifeProfile` (Decision 9). Loading still fails clearly on a profile without one.
- [ ] Restore (Decision 4): a Store operation that erases every table and imports a backup document in one transaction, so a bad file leaves the old data in place. `GRDBBackup.import` keeps its empty-database rule.
- [ ] `GRDBBackup` joins `AppServices` behind a small protocol in Core, so Settings doesn't see GRDB.
- [ ] **New product and its first lot in one transaction.** A repository call (protocol in Core, implementation in Store) that inserts a new product and a lot of it together; if either insert fails, neither is saved. The Add flow (Task 8) uses it whenever the product is new, and Slice 4's scanner reuses it unchanged.

**Tests:** the notice window round-trips through the site repository and the backup; a version 1 backup imports with 30 days; delete a lot with an override and both are gone; delete a kit and its location can then be deleted; every bundled profile has a non-empty name; restore over a populated database leaves exactly the file's contents; a restore that fails partway leaves the original data intact; export → restore → export matches apart from `exportedAt`; adding a new product with its lot writes both, and a lot that fails validation leaves no product behind.

**Done when:** every write the screens need exists as a repository call.
close_reason: v2 notice window + backup v2, lot/kit delete, product+lot txn, recent products, unit-kind lock, profile names, restore + BackupService; 297 tests

title: Slice 3 · Task 2 — Focus next in Core
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 2: Focus next in Core

- [ ] A Core function that builds the Focus next list from a `SiteRunway` and the Task 1 statuses, in the spec's priority order, for items 1 and 2 only:
  1. The limiting category with the amount needed to reach the next target, in the category's natural unit ("+18 gal water to reach 14 days", "+42,000 kcal food to reach 14 days"). Expressed as data (category, amount, unit, target days); wording is the app's job.
  2. Lots in Caution or Inspect, soonest usable-by first, then Use soon lots by printed date; ties broken by product name.
- [ ] Runway problems that stop the math (no occupants) come first as their own item; lots missing nutrition or water volume appear as one item each with their count.
- [ ] Items 3–5 (missing capabilities, kit gaps, maintenance) are not built; the type leaves room for them.

**Tests:** limiting-category item uses the next target's shortfall; no item 1 when the effective low is already past the last target; Caution and Inspect ordered by usable-by, followed by Use soon by printed date; expired lots aren't listed as "eat or rotate"; zero occupants puts the problem first; the fixture produces the expected list.

**Done when:** the Dashboard can render Focus next without deciding anything itself.
close_reason: FocusNext.items (items 1-2 + problems, missing data); 264 tests

title: Slice 3 · Task 3 — Inventory query in Core
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 3: Inventory query in Core

- [ ] Group the Task 1 statuses by location (full path, parents before children, kits marked) or by category, with lots inside each group ordered by state severity (Expired, Inspect, Caution, Use soon, Good) then usable-by.
- [ ] Search matches product name or lot notes, ignoring case and diacritics.
- [ ] Filters: expiring soon (Decision 7), and one category (for the Dashboard's drill-in). Filters and search combine.

**Tests:** table-driven grouping and ordering over the fixture; search hits name and notes; expiring soon includes Use soon, Caution and Inspect and leaves out Good and Expired; category filter plus search together; an empty result is an empty list, not an error.

**Done when:** Inventory's view model is a subscription plus one call to this function.
close_reason: Inventory.sections: grouping, severity order, search, filters; 274 tests

title: Slice 3 · Task 1 — Per-lot status in Core
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md → Task 1: Per-lot status in Core

The Inventory and the Focus next list need each lot's state, and that state must be exactly what the runway used. Today that logic is private to `RunwayCalculator`.

- [ ] A Core function that takes `RunwayInputs`, the profile table and `today`, and returns a status per unarchived lot: the lot, its product, its location chain (for a "Garage › Shelf 2" path), resolved climate and humidity, the `ShelfLifeEvaluation` (state, usable-by, flags), and whether it counts toward this site's runway (kit exclusion included). Lots the runway can't place (missing product, unresolved location, missing profile) come back with that problem rather than being dropped.
- [ ] **Use soon** (spec, shelf-life state table): `LotState.useSoon` for a lot within the notice window before its printed date. Best-by lots go Good → Use soon → Caution → Inspect → Expired; use-by lots skip Caution and Inspect (Good → Use soon → Expired). A lot with no printed date is Good. `ShelfLifeEvaluator.evaluate` takes the notice window as a parameter.
- [ ] `Site` gains the notice window in days (default 30, a positive whole number). Persisting it is Task 4.
- [ ] `RunwayCalculator` uses this function for its own per-lot step, so the two can't drift. Use soon lots count toward both the low and the high end, so the fixture's food and water low/high values don't change.

**Tests:** the fixture's lots get the states the Slice 1 tests imply (re-derived by hand where a Good lot is now Use soon) (the 14-month-old beans, the go-bag MRE excluded from runway, the Mylar beans with no printed date flagged `missingDate`); a lot at another site is absent; a missing product is reported, not dropped; the fixture runway test passes unchanged. Table-driven Use soon boundaries: the day the window opens, the printed date itself, a use-by lot moving from Use soon straight to Expired, and a window of a different length. Use soon lots count in the low end.

**Done when:** every lot state the UI shows comes from this one function.
close_reason: LotStatusEvaluator + Use soon state; RunwayCalculator counts from it; 255 tests

title: Slice 3: first real UI (manual entry)
description:
Source: docs/slice-3.md

**Goal:** Hampton can enter his real pantry by hand on the phone and read the answer back. After this slice the app has a Dashboard that shows food, water and effective runway as a low–high range with the top of the Focus next list, an Inventory that lists every lot with its shelf-life state and lets him use up, adjust, edit or delete it, an Add flow that creates a lot (and a product, if new) quickly with any expiry date past or future, and Settings for the household, locations and backup. Barcode scanning comes next; this slice proves the screens, the view-model pattern and the entry fields against real shelves first.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (Architecture rules, Working style), docs/design.md (color tokens, text styles, SF Symbols, components, and the "Slice 3: manual entry" row of the design canvas for this slice's screens), docs/spec.md → the shelf-life state table (including **Use soon**), **Runway dashboard**, **Screens and flows** and **Data model** (Units, Consumption, Shelf life), and the Slice 1–2 code: `RunwayCalculator`, `ShelfLifeEvaluator`, `ShelfLifeProfileResolver`, `resolvedClimate`, the repository protocols in `Repositories.swift`, `GRDBBackup`, and the app target (`AppServices`, `RootView`, `ContentView`, `SamplePantry`).

**Slices 1 and 2 are the ground truth for type names and shapes.** Where this file names a type or field differently from the code, follow the code and mention the difference in your plan. If a Core or Store type needs to change, list it in the plan before touching it.

Start in plan mode: propose the new Core types (per-lot status, Focus next, inventory query), the Store additions, the screen and view-model list with file layout, and the test plan, then wait for approval. Work the tasks in dependency order and commit after each task.

**View models subscribe, they don't poll.** Every screen that shows site data is driven by `RunwayInputsLoader.observeRunwayInputs(siteID:)` (or `LotRepository.observeLots(siteID:)` where lots alone are enough), as Slice 2 set up. Writes go through the repository protocols; the observation brings the new state back. No screen keeps its own copy of the data and patches it after a save.

**Logic lives in HearthstockCore, not in views.** Anything that decides what to show (a lot's state, the Focus next order, what "expiring soon" means, grouping and search) is a pure, tested Core function that takes `today` as a parameter. View models are `@MainActor @Observable` and stay thin: subscribe, call Core, format. There is no app test target in this slice, so whatever isn't in Core is verified by hand.

## Decisions taken in this plan

These are defaults chosen where the spec leaves a choice open. Hampton can overturn any of them before this goes into Beads.

1. **Manual entry only.** VisionKit barcode scanning, Live Text dates, Open Food Facts and pantry walk mode are Slice 4. The Add flow opens on manual entry, and the spec's "camera opens by default" arrives with the scanner. A barcode can still be typed into the product form.
2. **Three tabs now: Dashboard, Inventory, Settings.** Kits and Tasks tabs arrive with the slices that give them content, so no tab is a placeholder. Add is a toolbar button on Dashboard and Inventory.
3. **Days are shown as whole days, rounded down** ("12–19 days"; "under 1 day" below 1; a single number when both ends round the same). Core keeps returning unrounded `Double`s.
4. **Backup restore replaces everything.** `GRDBBackup.import` only fills an empty database, and the app always has the default site, so restore becomes "erase and import" in one transaction, behind a confirmation that says what will be lost and offers to export first.
5. **A lot can be deleted** (for entry mistakes), separately from using it up. Using it up archives at zero, as Slice 2 built; delete removes the row and its shelf-life override.
6. **Calories are entered per base unit, with a per-package helper.** The product form shows "kcal per lb" (or per count, per gal) and offers "kcal per package + package size" that converts on entry. Only the per-base-unit value is stored.
7. **Use soon is a real lot state, and its notice window is stored on the site.** The spec's Use soon state (within the notice window before the printed date) is added to `LotState` in Task 1. The window defaults to 30 days, is stored per site (the spec's "per household"), and is edited in Settings. "Expiring soon" in Inventory means Use soon, Caution or Inspect, as the spec says.
8. **Last-used location** is remembered per site in `UserDefaults`. It's a UI convenience, not domain data, so it stays out of the database and the backup.
9. **Shelf-life profiles get display names in the bundled JSON** (a `name` field per profile), so the product form's picker reads as words, not keys. Defaults stay data.
10. **Kits are a toggle on a location** in this slice ("This is a kit", plus "Counts toward runway", off by default). Templates, inspection and the Kits tab are later.

## Out of scope for this slice

Barcode and Live Text scanning, Open Food Facts lookup, pantry walk mode (Slice 4); the Kits and Tasks tabs, kit templates and gap checking, readiness templates, maintenance tasks; capabilities and water treatment, power runway, cooking fuel; Focus next items 3–5; editing targets, climate multipliers or the shelf-life table in Settings (per-product and per-lot overrides included); a site switcher or a second site in the UI; notifications, widgets, App Intents; CSV export; CloudKit sync.

## Definition of done

- `swift test` green; report the test count, including every Slice 1 and Slice 2 test. The sample-pantry fixture test and its Store round-trip must still pass with unchanged expected values.
- `xcodegen generate` and the `xcodebuild` build (Debug and Release) both succeed.
- HearthstockCore still imports only Foundation; no view or view model imports GRDB or HearthstockStore apart from `AppServices`.
- Hampton has walked the Task 12 script on the simulator and confirmed each step.
- The summary lists the screens and view models, the new Core and Store API, every assumption made, and any Slice 1–2 types changed and why.

title: Slice 2 · Task 8 — JSON export and import
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 8 — JSON export and import

Backup before real data goes in.

- [ ] Export: the whole database to one versioned JSON document (`{"formatVersion": 1, "exportedAt": …, "sites": […], …}`), with dates as ISO strings.
- [ ] Import: into an empty database only (fail with a typed error otherwise), all inside one transaction, so a failed import leaves nothing behind.
- [ ] Export → import → export produces identical JSON, apart from `exportedAt`.

**Tests:** the round-trip above using the sample pantry; importing into a non-empty database fails cleanly; a file with an unknown formatVersion fails cleanly.
close_reason: JSON export/import (GRDBBackup), versioned doc, transactional import into empty DB; 240 tests green

title: Slice 2 · Task 9 — App wiring
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 9 — App wiring

- [ ] At launch, open the on-disk database, run migrations, and call `ensureDefaultSite()`. Pass repositories to SwiftUI through the environment.
- [ ] `ContentView` shows the site name, lot count, and the effective runway range as plain text. It's a smoke test, not real UI.
- [ ] A **DEBUG-only** "Load sample pantry" button that imports the fixture into an empty database, for development on the simulator.
- [ ] If the database fails to open or migrate, show the error text on screen instead of crashing.

**Done when:** you tell me what to tap in the simulator and what I should see, and I confirm it.
notes: Closed: App wiring (on-disk DB at launch, environment repositories, smoke ContentView, DEBUG sample loader, error screen). swift test 240 passing; xcodegen + Debug/Release builds OK; verified on iPhone 17 simulator.
close_reason: App wiring: on-disk DB at launch, env repositories, smoke ContentView, DEBUG sample loader, error screen; swift test 240 passing; xcodegen + Debug/Release builds OK; verified on iPhone 17 simulator

title: Slice 2 · Task 7 — Fixture round-trip (main regression test)
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 7 — Fixture round-trip (main regression test)

- [ ] Load Slice 1's `sample-pantry` fixture into an in-memory database through the repositories, not raw SQL.
- [ ] Load it back with the `RunwayInputs` loader, run `RunwayCalculator`, and assert the same food and water low/high values the Slice 1 fixture test asserts.

This test proves the database adds nothing and loses nothing. It must stay green in every future slice.
close_reason: Fixture round-trip through repositories and loader matches Slice 1 runway; 229 tests green

title: Slice 2 · Task 5 — Observation
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 5 — Observation

- [ ] `observeRunwayInputs(siteID:) -> AsyncThrowingStream<RunwayInputs, Error>` and `observeLots(siteID:)`, built on GRDB `ValueObservation`. These are what Slice 3's view models subscribe to.
- [ ] The stream emits the current value immediately, then again after each relevant write.

**Tests:** subscribe, save a lot, and receive an updated value; a write to another site doesn't change this site's values.
close_reason: observeRunwayInputs/observeLots via ValueObservation; 171 tests green

title: Slice 2 · Task 6 — Shelf-life and climate overrides
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 6 — Shelf-life and climate overrides

Per the spec's Decisions, the bundled shelf-life table is a default the user can edit per product and per lot.

- [ ] `ShelfLifeProfileResolver` in Core resolves a profile in this order: lot override, then product override, then bundled default by key. Each override field falls back individually, so overriding only extensionMonths keeps the rest of the default.
- [ ] A location's `climateMultiplierOverride`, when set, replaces its climate class multiplier.
- [ ] The repository exposes overrides for saving and clearing; `RunwayInputs` includes them.

**Tests:** each level of the resolution order; partial overrides; a location multiplier override changing a lot's state on the boundary day.
close_reason: Shelf-life/climate overrides: resolver, location multiplier, override repository, RunwayInputs; 226 tests green

title: Slice 2 · Task 3 — Records and mapping
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 3 — Records and mapping

- [ ] GRDB record structs in `HearthstockStore` (`SiteRecord`, `LotRecord`, and so on) that conform to `FetchableRecord` and `PersistableRecord`, with explicit mapping to and from the Core value types.
- [ ] Don't conform Core types to GRDB protocols, even retroactively. Core stays free of GRDB.
- [ ] `updatedAt` is set on every write; `createdAt` only on insert. The current time comes from an injectable clock, never `Date()` inline, so tests stay deterministic.

**Tests:** a round-trip for every entity (Core → record → database → record → Core is equal), including nil optionals, every enum case, and dates at month and year boundaries.
close_reason: GRDB records and Core mapping for site, person, location, kit, product and lot; StoreClock; stamped writes; 135 tests green

title: Slice 2 · Task 4 — Repository protocols and implementations
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 4 — Repository protocols and implementations

- [ ] Protocols live in `HearthstockCore`; GRDB implementations live in `HearthstockStore`. Every method is `async throws`, and every protocol is `Sendable`.
- [ ] `SiteRepository`: list, get, save, ensureDefaultSite() (idempotent; creates "Home" if no site exists).
- [ ] `PersonRepository`: list(siteID), save, delete.
- [ ] `LocationRepository`: list(siteID), save, delete. Deleting a location that still has lots fails with a typed error.
- [ ] `ProductRepository`: get, find(barcode:), search(name:), save.
- [ ] `LotRepository`: list(siteID, includeArchived:), save, consume(lotID, amount) (reduces the quantity and archives the lot when it reaches zero; consuming more than is left is a typed error), archive.
- [ ] `KitRepository`: list(siteID), save.
- [ ] `RunwayInputs` loader: one read transaction returning everything `RunwayCalculator` needs for a site, so the dashboard never sees a half-written state.

title: Slice 2 · Task 2 — Migration `v1_initial`
description:
Source: docs/slice-2.md → Task 2 — Migration `v1_initial`

Tables for what Slice 1 models. Conventions:

- Primary keys are UUID strings (`TEXT`). No autoincrement integers; this keeps CloudKit sync possible later.
- Calendar dates are `TEXT` in ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Enums are `TEXT` raw values, with a `CHECK` constraint listing the allowed values.
- Every table has `createdAt` and `updatedAt` (`TEXT`, ISO-8601 timestamps with UTC). These are metadata for future sync, not domain data.
- Quantities are `REAL` in base units, with `CHECK (quantity >= 0)`.

| Table | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `site` | name |
| `person` | siteId → site (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), name, kcalPerDay, waterGalPerDay |
| `location` | siteId → site, parentId → location (nullable), name, climateClass?, climateMultiplierOverride?, humidity?, kitId? |
| `kit` | homeSiteId → site, locationId → location, templateKey?, countsTowardSiteRunway (default 0), lastInspected? |
| `product` | name, barcode (unique where not null), category, role, baseUnit, kcalPerBaseUnit?, potableWaterGalPerBaseUnit?, isNonPotable, shelfLifeProfileKey |
| `lot` | siteId → site, productId → product, locationId → location, quantity, acquiredDate, printedDate?, packaging, climateOverride?, opened, archived, notes? |
| `shelf_life_override` | productId? or lotId? (exactly one, enforced by `CHECK`), dateType?, extensionMonths?, packagedLifeMonths?, rotationMonths? |

- [ ] Foreign keys are `ON DELETE RESTRICT` unless noted. Deleting a product that still has lots must fail, not cascade.
- [ ] `lot.siteId` must equal its location's site. Enforce this with a trigger, not only in Swift, so a bad write can't corrupt a site's runway.
- [ ] Indexes: `lot(siteId, archived)`, `lot(productId)`, `lot(locationId)`, `location(siteId)`, `product(barcode)`.

**Tests:** each `CHECK` rejects a bad value; the site-mismatch trigger rejects a mismatched lot; deleting a product with lots fails; deleting a site cascades its persons.
close_reason: v1_initial: 7 tables, 7 triggers, indexes; swift test green, 101 tests

title: Slice 1 · Task 6 — Runway calculator
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md → Task 6 — Runway calculator

- [ ] `RunwayCalculator.runway(for site, occupants, lots, products, locations, kits, profiles, on today) -> SiteRunway`.
- [ ] Only lots whose location resolves to this site. Exclude archived lots and lots inside kits with `countsTowardSiteRunway == false`.
- [ ] Food: `low` = kcal from `.good` lots ÷ Σ occupants' kcalPerDay; `high` adds `.caution` and `.inspect`. Expired never counts.
- [ ] Water: same low/high split over potable gallons. Lots tagged non-potable are reported separately as `untreatedNonPotableGal` and not counted (treatment arrives in v1.1).
- [ ] Effective runway = min of food and water, for low and high separately; `limitingCategory` = category that sets the low end.
- [ ] Next target: the first of 3, 14, 30 days above the effective low; report the shortfall for the limiting category in its base unit (kcal or gal).
- [ ] Problems are returned, not thrown: zero occupants → `.noOccupants`; food lots with no kcal data → listed in `lotsMissingNutrition` and excluded.
- [ ] Days are `Double`; no rounding in HearthstockCore.

**Tests:** single-person basics; two people with different kcal targets; caution lots raise only the high end; go-bag excluded by default and included when the flag is on; a lot at another site ignored; zero occupants; missing-kcal lot reported.

**Fixture:** `Fixtures/sample-pantry.json` — one site, two adults (2,400 and 2,000 kcal/day), ~15 realistic lots across a hot garage, a cool-dry closet and a go-bag: e.g. 20 lb white rice (garage), 6 cans black beans with a printed date 14 months ago, a 24-pack of 0.5 L bottled water, 5 gal stored tap water acquired 8 months ago, Mylar-packed beans with no printed date, flour, peanut butter, honey, an MRE in the go-bag. Write the expected food/water low/high values in a comment, computed by hand, and assert them. I'll swap in my real pantry later; the test should keep working with new expected values.
close_reason: RunwayCalculator with food/water low-high, kit/site exclusion, targets, sample pantry fixture; 82 tests green

title: Slice 1 · Task 5 — Shelf-life evaluation
description:
Source: docs/slice-1.md → Task 5 — Shelf-life evaluation

- [ ] `ShelfLifeEvaluator.state(of lot, product, profile, climate, on today: CalendarDate) -> LotState` returning `.good`, `.caution`, `.inspect`, `.expired`, plus the computed `usableBy: CalendarDate?`.
- [ ] Rules (spec → Shelf life and Storage climate):
  - `useBy`: good through the printed date, expired after it. No extension, no climate scaling.
  - `bestBy` with printed date: good through printed date; window = extensionMonths × climate multiplier (round down to whole days); caution until the last 20% of the window; inspect for the last 20%; expired after.
  - Packaging `mylarO2`/`bucket` with `packagedLifeMonths`: usable-by = acquired + packagedLifeMonths × climate multiplier. Use whichever of this and the printed-date rule is **later**.
  - No printed date + `rotationMonths`: usable-by = acquired + rotationMonths (no climate scaling); good until the last 20%, then inspect, then expired.
  - `none` with no rotation: always good.
  - No printed date and none of the above: good, and flagged `missingDate` so the UI can nudge later.
  - Refrigerated/frozen climate: out of scope for this slice — evaluate as climateControlled and flag `powerDependent`.
- [ ] Humidity flag: a humid location adds `humidityRisk` to lots whose packaging is `none` (cans, paper, cardboard). It doesn't change dates.

**Tests (table-driven):** each date type; boundary days (exactly on printed date, first caution day, first inspect day, first expired day); hot garage (0.5×) vs cool-dry (1.25×) for the same can; Mylar rice with an old printed date still good; use-by formula one day past → expired; stored tap water at 5 and 7 months.
close_reason: ShelfLifeEvaluator: best-by/use-by/packaged/rotation rules, climate scaling, missingDate/powerDependent/humidityRisk flags; 65 tests green
